dedupe_keys.name: demand for ports to 2050 climate policy trade growth and sea level rise shipping in changing climates

description: This dataset from the Shipping in Changing Climates (SCC) research consortium gives decadal estimates, from 2010 to 2050, of the port area needed to handle projected seaborne trade under four climate-related policy scenarios. It also includes projections of relative sea-level rise and cost estimates both for adapting ports to the anticipated rise under each scenario and for building any new port area required. It was produced by S. E. Hanson (University of Southampton) and R. J. Nicholls (University of East Anglia), and the method is described in Hanson and Nicholls (2020). Coverage is global. The data are numeric tables deposited with the UK Data Service (2020); they are available to download without registration, and commercial use is not permitted. Caveats: the estimates depend on the trade and policy scenarios, are decadal and aggregated, not port by port designs, and costs carry the assumptions of the method paper. They support long-term capacity planning and climate adaptation of port infrastructure under sea-level rise. They complement the UNCTAD maritime statistics and are related to global port location databases.
